'''Shisho Shrine''' (四所神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Fukushima|en|Fukushima|qid=Q230656|lt=Fukushima (Tokushima City)}}, {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|qid=Q207309|lt=Tokushima}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|qid=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture}}. It has been designated a {{ill|Q11273094|ja|とくしま市民遺産|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Citizen Heritage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11273094}}.
== Overview ==
The origins of Shisho Shrine date back to 807 (Daido 2), according to tradition (see {{ill|Folklore|en|Folklore|qid=Q36192|lt=Legend}}). It is one of the five notable shrines of central Tokushima. 
Historically known as Shisho Myojin or Shisho Daimyojin, the shrine is affectionately called "Fukushima Myojin" by locals. 
There is a legend that a serpent resides within the shrine, though the details were nearly forgotten. Recently discovered ancient documents revealed that two sacred {{ill|Dragon Serpents|ja|龍蛇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dragon Serpents|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|en|Izumo-taisha|qid=Q696362|lt=Izumo Taisha}} are enshrined here. In 1788 (Tenmei 8), the {{ill|Dragon Serpents|ja|龍蛇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dragon Serpents|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} were delivered to the Tokushima Domain from Izumo Taisha. Revering their divine power, the domain enshrined them in Shisho Shrine, where they were venerated during ceremonial voyages. 
Two years later, in 1790 (Kansei 2), another Dragon Serpent brought by the naval commander Mori Jingobei was also enshrined. It was recorded in ''Zoku Awa Kuni Choko Zassho'' that the first serpent was male, while the second was female, forming a mystical pair.
In 2024 (Reiwa 6), the shrine began holding the {{ill|Dragon Serpent Festival|ja|龍蛇神祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dragon Serpent Festival|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. 
The shrine grounds include a literary monument dedicated to the novelist [[:en:Unno Juza|Unno Juza]], who grew up in the area. The shrine is also connected to {{ill|Hana Kaifu|ja|海部ハナ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana Kaifu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11559318}}.
== Festivals ==
* {{ill|January 1|en|January 1|qid=Q2150|lt=January 1}} - New Year Festival
* {{ill|May 15|en|May 15|qid=Q2562|lt=May 15}} - Taidai Kagura Festival
* {{ill|July 8|en|July 8|qid=Q2692|lt=July 8}}, {{ill|July 9|en|July 9|qid=Q2690|lt=July 9}} - Summer Festival
* {{ill|October 27|en|October 27|qid=Q2956|lt=October 27}}, {{ill|October 28|en|October 28|qid=Q2952|lt=October 28}} - Autumn Festival (with ''Chōsa'' portable shrine)

== Legend ==
A legend recounts that in the offshore area of Tokushima City's {{ill|Q11556321|ja|津田町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuda Town|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11556321}}, there was once an island called Kamejima, where a shrine adorned with two deer statues stood. An elderly couple visited the shrine daily until they dreamt of a deity warning, "When the deer’s eyes turn red, the island will sink; take the deer and flee." A young pRankster painted the deer’s eyes red, prompting the couple to flee with the statues. That night, a great tsunami submerged the island. Grateful for their rescue, the couple enshrined the deer at Shisho Shrine.

== Access ==
* Approximately 5 minutes by car from {{ill|Tokushima Station|en|Tokushima Station|qid=Q860775|lt=Tokushima Station}} (JR).
* Near "Fukushima Myojin-mae" bus stop on {{ill|Tokushima City Transportation Bureau|ja|徳島市営バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Bus|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳島市交通局|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11489713}} routes to Okisumura and Nankai Ferry.
